title: SQLite | Node.js v24 documentation
claims: The node:sqlite module ships inside Node 24 without the --experimental-sqlite flag and is documented at Stability 1.2 - Release candidate as of v24.15.0.

It exposes synchronous DatabaseSync and StatementSync classes with open, readOnly, timeout, foreign-key and defensive options plus a module-level backup() function, and has no transaction helper, so BEGIN and COMMIT are issued as SQL.
notes: API surface only. Class names differ across release lines (DatabaseSync on v24, a Database alias in later docs), so the exact pinned Node minor matters. No Splyce durability, crash or timing result is implied.

title: better-sqlite3 API documentation
claims: better-sqlite3 provides a synchronous API with transaction() wrappers (deferred, immediate, exclusive and nested savepoints), pragma(), and a promise-returning backup().

Its documented caveats are that manual BEGIN/COMMIT must not be mixed with transaction(), and that SQLite may roll a transaction back on errors such as SQLITE_FULL or SQLITE_BUSY, leaving callers to check the in-transaction flag after catching.
notes: Library documentation. The repository's performance table is a vendor benchmark, not a Splyce measurement, and is not used for selection here.

title: better-sqlite3 npm registry metadata
claims: The published release 13.0.3 is MIT-licensed, requires Node >=22, declares node-addon-api ^8, and carries no npm install or build script in its metadata (gypfile false).
notes: Metadata only. Prebuilt-binary contents and an actual Windows x64 load are unverified until TD-09 runs the candidate on the target platform.

title: Write-Ahead Logging
claims: In WAL mode writers sync the WAL on every commit when PRAGMA synchronous is FULL, and omit that sync when it is NORMAL, so NORMAL commits may roll back after a power loss or hard reset.
WAL requires all processes to share memory on one host and cannot run on a network filesystem, and a database file separated from its -wal file can lose committed transactions or corrupt.
notes: Engine-level durability semantics. It does not establish that a Node binding exposes or preserves them, and no Splyce trial was run.

title: How To Corrupt An SQLite Database File
claims: SQLite automatically rolls back a partially written transaction on the next access after an application crash, OS crash or power failure.

A copy taken while a transaction is in flight can be inconsistent, while the backup API, VACUUM INTO or a copy with no transaction in flight is safe, and hot -journal or -wal files must travel with the database.
notes: Recovery and copy-safety guidance. It is not evidence about our binding, our kill sequence or Windows filesystem behaviour.
